_comment: Hand-maintained patches merged into schema.json by generate-schema.js. Use only for values the static parser cannot resolve (enum-derived choices and defaults, descriptions missing upstream, source-expression defaultText made human-readable). Keep entries minimal and verify against neonctl source when refreshing the schema pin.

help.describe: Show help for a command or subcommand

api-key.describe: Neon API key, authenticates without `neon auth`

context-file.describe: Context file with default org, project, and branch IDs, created by `neon link`
context-file.defaultText: nearest .neon file, searching upward from the current directory

env-pull.describe: Pull the branch's Neon env vars (DATABASE_URL, ...) into a local .env after checkout. On by default; use --no-env-pull to skip, for example when injecting env at runtime with `neon-env run` (from `@neon/env`) or `neon dev`.

profile._comment: Limit the table to the two common create paths (browser sign-in, then --mint). The upstream `.example()` list also demonstrates storing a pre-existing key via --api-key; that rarer path and its stdin/argument trade-off are covered in prose on the page instead. Same commands and descriptions as source (profile.ts) for the examples kept.

examples.description: Sign in with the browser, like `neon auth --profile work`
One browser sign-in, then an org-scoped key and no session left behind

env-pull.describe: Pull the linked branch's Neon env vars (DATABASE_URL, ...) into a local .env after linking. On by default; use --no-env-pull to skip, for example when injecting env at runtime with `neon-env run` (from `@neon/env`) or `neon dev`.

hipaa.describe: Enable HIPAA compliance for the project.
Enable HIPAA compliance for the project.

provider-id.describe: OAuth provider ID. Supported values: google, github, vercel
OAuth provider ID. Supported values: google, github, vercel
OAuth provider ID. Supported values: google, github, vercel

frequency.describe: How often to take snapshots. Combine with --hour, --day, and --retention to build a single-entry schedule.
